quick_notes.title: Ancient/Medieval Recap
quick_notes.detail: Sangam (3rd Madurai). Thinai (Kurinji: Mountain). Silappathikaram (Ilango). Pallava (Vichitrachitta). Chola (Big Temple/Uttiramerur (Parantaka I)). Pandyas (Marco Polo).
quick_notes.explanation: Sangam refers to a gathering of poets in ancient South India, with the third and most famous Sangam held in the city of Madurai. Thinai is a Tamil word for a type of landscape, and Kurinji specifically means the mountainous region where lovers would meet in secret. Silappathikaram is a famous Tamil epic poem written by the prince Ilango Adigal, telling the story of a woman named Kannagi. The Pallava dynasty, with a notable king named Vichitrachitta, ruled parts of South India and were known for their rock-cut temples. The Chola dynasty, under the king Parantaka I, built the Brihadeeswarar Temple, also called the Big Temple, and created the Uttiramerur inscriptions which describe rules for local village elections. The Pandya dynasty was visited by the Italian traveler Marco Polo, who wrote about their wealth and the pearl fishing along their coast.

quick_notes.title: Revolt Recap
quick_notes.detail: Puli Thevar (1st). Kattabomman (Hanged Kayathar). Marudu (Lion of Sivagangai). 1806 (Vellore Mutiny).
quick_notes.explanation: Puli Thevar was the first leader in Tamil Nadu to fight against British rule in the 1750s. Kattabomman was a Tamil chieftain who was captured and hanged by the British at Kayathar in 1799 for refusing to pay taxes. The Marudu brothers, known as the Lions of Sivagangai, led a rebellion against the British in 1801 and were executed. In 1806, the Vellore Mutiny was an uprising by Indian soldiers (sepoys) in Vellore Fort against new British military rules that violated their religious customs.

quick_notes.title: Leaders Recap
quick_notes.detail: VOC (SSN Company). Bharati (National Poet). Vanchinathan (Ashe Murder). MMS (1884).
quick_notes.explanation: The VOC refers to V.O. Chidambaram Pillai, who founded the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company (SSN Company) in 1906 to compete with British shipping lines. Bharati is Subramania Bharati, a Tamil poet and independence activist who is honored as the National Poet of India for his patriotic songs and writings. Vanchinathan was a revolutionary who assassinated British collector Robert Ashe in 1911 to protest British rule. MMS stands for Madras Mahajana Sabha, a political organization formed in 1884 that worked for Indian representation and rights before the Indian National Congress was created.

quick_notes.title: Sites Recap
quick_notes.explanation: Keezhadi is an archaeological site near the Vaigai River in Tamil Nadu where excavations have found evidence of an ancient urban settlement from the Sangam period. Adichanallur is a site in Tamil Nadu known for its urn burials, which are clay pots used to hold the bones or ashes of dead people from the Iron Age. Mahabalipuram is a town on the coast of Tamil Nadu famous for its stone temples and sculptures built by the Pallava kings, who ruled from the 3rd to 9th centuries. Gangaikondacholapuram is a town in Tamil Nadu where the Chola king Rajendra I built a grand temple to celebrate his victory over the Ganges region.

quick_notes.title: Literary Recap
quick_notes.explanation: The literary works known as Ettuthogai, meaning the Eight Anthologies, are a collection of eight books of short poems from the Sangam period of ancient Tamil literature. The Pathupattu, meaning the Ten Idylls, is a set of ten longer poems also from the same Sangam era. Together, these eighteen works form the core of Sangam poetry. The Twin Epics refer to two great Tamil epic poems: Silappathikaram, which tells the story of the merchant Kovalan and his wife Kannagi, and Manimegalai, which continues the story with their daughter. Both epics are important works of Tamil literature written after the Sangam period.

lesson_intro: Today we consolidate the 'Glory and Struggle of Tamil Nadu'. You have mastered the Sangam era, the Pallava/Chola/Pandya empires, and the early phase of the freedom fight. In TNPSC, Unit 8 is the 'Mark Machine'. Today, we drill the titles, the years, and the sites. If you see 'Uttiramerur (Parantaka I)', you say 'Chola Admin'. If you see 'Kayathar', you say 'Kattabomman'. Let's lock in the Unit 8 marks today.
